36 New Books Out November 10, 2026

By BookBub
•
November 09, 2026
•
10 min read
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 30:13
Instaread

Every Tuesday publishers releases tens of new books out into the world. Here are the new books hitting shelves today, November 10! From book club picks, to cozy fantasy, to simmering romance, there’s a reason for you to buying a new book today. 

The First House

Avni Doshi

When her husband abruptly ends their 13-year marriage, a woman is left to rebuild her life with their two children while questioning everything she thought she knew about their relationship and her own family. As old tensions resurface and strange events unsettle her, she begins a painful journey toward understanding what was lost — and imagining what might come next. Rumaan Alam says The First House is a “beautiful book that delights in resisting its readers’ expectations.”

The Man Who Read Books

Rachid Benzine

Barnes & Noble Best Fiction of 2026

An elderly bookseller improbably keeps his shop open in Palestine, telling a foreign correspondent the ways in which literature has provided him with refuge and inspiration.

“An essential novel to remind us that those in Gaza continue to read, they continue to exist.” --David Diop, author of Beyond the Door of No Return and At Night All Blood Is Black

A young French photographer travels to Palestine to report on the bombings in the Gaza Strip. One morning, during a ceasefire, he wanders far from his hotel into the narrow alleys of the city. Roaming aimlessly, he stumbles across a bookseller sitting on the doorstop of his shop--an old man, surrounded by stacks of books. As the photographer raises his camera, the bookseller calls out to him and asks him to listen to his story, not simply take his picture.

The story that unfolds is one that encompasses exile and imprisonment, activism and political disillusionment, the joys of love and art and watching your children grow up and thrive, and the tragedies that tear your loved ones from you. Each event is tied to the book that helped him understand and, in some cases, survive it, from Milan Kundera to Frantz Fanon to Umberto Eco to Ernest Hemingway, among many others.

There’s a saying that when an old man dies a library burns, and it’s this very library that the bookseller opens and describes. Rachid Benzine gives us a magnificent modern tale that explores the power of words against barbarism, of books as the last bastions of resistance against the loss of empathy, of literature as a means of sustenance during our darkest hours.

Don’t Stop Snowing

Gabriel Bump

A deeply personal and funny novel from the winner of the Ernest J. Gaines Award, about embracing one’s own troubled self, demons and all. Perfect for readers of Percival Everett, Kevin Wilson, and Brandon Taylor’s The Late Americans.

Fresh out of grad school in Michigan, on the brink of despair, directionless, David worries his parents. They don’t know how to heal him. His doctor suggests that he needs to gain some perspective, and possibly a relocation would help. Maybe there is such a thing as a geographical cure?

Snowy, grey Buffalo is not the first place that comes to mind when you think of a curative place, but maybe time with his cousin Flip will help David to forget his own troubled past. But as it turns out, Flip’s life and state of mind is even unsteadier than his own. Suddenly enlisted to take care of his cousin and to even fill in for him at his job, David falls into a new life and a new way of seeing the world. A world where, come to think of it, he doesn’t mind the snow.

Don’t Stop Snowing is a fresh and honest--and funny--story of the struggles we all face as we realize that we don’t just inherit eye, hair, and skin color, but also the complicated psyches of our parents.

The Squatters

Saba Brelvi

Dalia Waheed has built a comfortable suburban life in Surrey, but volunteering with a refugee resettlement charity introduces her to Hajira, a pregnant asylum seeker living in dire conditions. When Dalia tries to help Hajira find a better place to live, her good intentions draw her into a political battle that threatens her marriage, friendships, and sense of community. Patmeena Sabit, author of Good People, says, “The Squatters is a beautiful, timely, and necessary novel.” 

This Impossible Life

Chinelo Okparanta

“Thunderous, magnificent...A new book by the brilliant Chinelo Okparanta is always cause for raucous celebration, and this is her masterpiece.”
-Karen Russell

“I simply could not put the book down...A wise and urgent voice in these impossible times.”
-Justin Torres

From the acclaimed author of Under the Udala Trees, a profoundly moving, unforgettable new epic following the aftermath of one catastrophic moment in the lives of two siblings.

Eleven-year-old Alohan and his four-year-old sister Ivie are the children of a rainmaker, who performs elaborate rituals to bring or hold back the rain. One day, the rainmaker’s luck runs out: it pours on the wrong person’s wedding, and the repercussions for him and for his wife who accompanies him to the wedding are deadly.

Orphaned and alone, Alohan is quickly forced into an early adulthood, charged with providing for and protecting Ivie. The two siblings become each other’s entire worlds, bound by loss and loyalty. But just as they begin to build a life for themselves, a lapse of judgment leaves them entangled with a wealthy couple’s nefarious scheme. The two are set on drastically different paths, constricted by the ruthlessness of those who hold great power and privilege, and those who are underfoot – who must, and will, do anything merely to survive.

What unfolds is an incredible journey of crime and betrayal, misunderstanding and misfortune, spanning continents and decades: from Nigeria to the United States to Italy, and from the homes of the wealthy elites, to those of the destitute—crossing paths, at each turn, with those who steal, con, and traffic in lives.

At the novel’s heart is the love between Alohan and Ivie. Told with captivating force, insight, and compassion, This Impossible Life is a gripping saga of two siblings’ survival, and of whether the love that binds them will be enough to overcome the most unforgiving of fates.

O Now!

Niall Williams

From novelist Niall Williams, bestselling author of Time of the Child and This Is Happiness, a new story set in the small Irish town of Faha, exploring love, loss, and the why of lifeMossie Crowe, known as Ganga, is that rare man who is beloved by everyone who knows him and is particularly cherished by his best friend, Bat. On one ordinary October day, Bat interrupts their usual evening tea to ask Ganga why God created the earth. But when Ganga passes away that night, Bat finds himself at a loss, without his friend and without an answer to his question. Over the next days, as all of Faha comes to care for and honor the body of the man they loved, Bat begins a new journey towards understanding life, death, and love.A tender exploration of life’s many meanings, O Now! is a perfect gift for readers who loved Niall Williams’ previous Faha novels and features an all-new essay from Niall exploring Faha’s creation and legacy.

No Such Thing As Monday

Siân Hughes

From a Booker Prize-longlisted author, a novel in which a woman tries to overcome her abusive past and find her estranged sister in a deeply moving and darkly humorous quest for redemption

Foul-mouthed, scrappy, and self-destructive, Steffie is her own worst enemy. Sustained by her sardonic sense of humor, she spends her days working at a dry cleaner and tending to her ailing, impoverished, abusive father. She was always his favorite, a fact that leaves her racked with guilt; her sister, Caroline, who bore the brunt of his rage, fled when they were both teenagers.

When her father dies, Steffie sets out to find Caroline, seeking love and forgiveness in a world that has too often denied her both. Along the way, she must confront her own memories, and the choices that have brought her to this point.

Written in the working-class British realist tradition of Douglas Stuart and Andrea Arnold, No Such Thing as Monday cements Siân Hughes’s reputation as an exceptional and compassionate chronicler of precarious and chaotic lives.

Crash into You

Simone Soltani

A forbidden love forces a shift in gears in the next sizzling Formula 1 romance from the USA Today bestselling author of Cross the Line.

Formula 1 driver Zaid Yousef is back—though he’s not sure he wants to be. After a crash last season left the seven-time world champion with two broken wrists and a hesitance to get back behind the wheel, his future in the sport is nothing short of uncertain. Saddled with an unfinished contract and expectations to win a record-shattering title, the only choice is for him to return . . . right?

The press turned Ava Farahani’s life upside down in the last few years, forcing her to leave her job in marketing and the world of F1 she grew up in. She knows she should stay far away from the track, but the draw of the sport she loves is too strong to resist. 

A preseason event brings the two together for one hot, reckless night, and weeks later, results in a positive pregnancy test. Ava desperately wants to be a mother, and the baby gives Zaid a newfound drive to survive the season and break the world record.

There’s just one little problem: Ava is a team principal’s daughter . . . and Zaid is their biggest rival.

Heartsworn

S.E. Wendel

Return to the world of Heartsong! A reclusive researcher gets the shock of a lifetime when the (very attractive) gargoyle statue in her rose garden awakens and claims her as his mate.

She’s known him all her life…

June Parkhurst is a prodigy, a conservator, and…an empath. Yet, her empathic abilities don’t feel like a gift; they’re a curse, one that’s driven her into isolation.

Overwhelmed by the feelings of others and her own grief, June sticks to what she loves most: statues. She’s always been fascinated by them, especially the gothic masterpiece in her family’s rose garden.

He’s watched over her for years…

For centuries, Alaric has despaired. Cursed to stone by the cruel Faerie Queen, Alaric has watched the world pass him by. He holds desperately onto a fleeting hope—that one day, June will come to understand what he’s known for years: she is his heartsong.

Magick stolen can be reclaimed, and curses cast can be broken…

A new museum with enigmatic owners has just opened, full of statues just like hers. Unable to resist, June emerges from seclusion determined to find answers about her statue. Yet, nothing is what it seems in this curious place, and June can’t ignore how…alive the statues feel.

The mysterious statues and their owners are just the start of the strangeness. During an attack by masked thieves, June swears one of the statues comes to life and flies away. But that’s impossible. As impossible as the whispers she hears from her beloved statue…mate.

Tropes:

• Monster romance

• Museum mystery

• Domestic bliss

• Protective monster mmc

• Nerdy fmc

• Neurodivergent fmc

• Healing/comfort over grief

• Fated mates

• Forced proximity

The Last Dragon Queen

Sylvia Mercedes

When love and loyalty spark, fire will forge the Dragon Queen’s destiny in this breathtaking conclusion to Sylvia Mercedes’s epic romantasy duology.

Rosie Harpwood never asked to be the Dragon Queen. But with Mhoryga’s darkness spreading and the fate of the realm at stake, she must embrace the terrifying magic in her blood. Alongside Prince Valtar—her former enemy and the man she now aches to trust—Rosie journeys into the wilds in search of a phoenix shrine that could awaken her full power. But claiming it may mean losing herself...and leaving Valtar behind for good. 

Far away, Rosie’s long-lost sister and Mhoryga’s most devoted creation, Nyxia, is hunting them down. Fierce and desperate to prove her worth, Nyxia will stop at nothing to carry out her mother’s will. But as doubts take root and forbidden feelings rise, Nyxia must choose between her creator and the one person who truly knows her. 

As passions entwine with flame and war ignites, Rosie, Valtar, and Nyxia hurtle toward a final reckoning where bonds will be tested, magic will burn, and nothing will ever be the same.

Loathed Love

Krista Ritchie and Becca Ritchie

Audrey Cobalt never expected a lie to land her between two men: the quiz bowl captain she wants and the bad-boy musician she hates.

The youngest of an accomplished family, Audrey Cobalt has spent her life chasing good grades and fantasizing over happily-ever-afters. Now fresh off to college and living with her older brothers, she’s determined to prove that New York City is where she’s fated to be.

Unfortunately...her dream life starts with a lie.

Guy Abernathy is cutthroat, ambitious, and the handsome captain of Manhattan Valley University’s prestigious quiz bowl team. He’s everything Audrey has always wanted.

Birdie St. Pierre is not.

He’s sharp-tongued, abrasive, and the hot musical prodigy who hates rich, spoiled heiresses. Tragic, since Birdie is her new tutor--and her only shot at staying on the quiz bowl team.

Whom does Audrey truly loathe, and whom does she truly love? It could be a Shakespearean mess if she finds out too late.

Wood You Be Mine?: A Grumpy Lumberjack Romance (Lovewell Lumberjacks Book 1)

Daphne Elliot

The first time I met the grumpy lumberjack next door, I almost burnt down his cabin. 

The second time, I was throwing tampons at a moose (don’t ask). 

The third time, I was naked. 

And Henri Gagnon is not just my neighbor and landlord, but a pain in my optimistic, plus sized ass. He’s got a protective streak under his grumpy exterior and he’s convinced I won’t make it through the Maine winter. 

I’m going to show him and the rest of this small town that they’re wrong. I have one year to prove myself as the new elementary school principal or I’ll be getting the ax. So I just don’t have time to pine away for the grumpy lumberjack next door, no matter how good he looks chopping wood in his suspenders or the way he growls when he calls me buttercup. 

But soon I’m falling headfirst down a hill, and into a full blown crush when he carries me home. He’s distracted trying to save his family’s lumber business, and I’ve got a school to run, and this small town is not as sleepy as it seems. But despite our differences, the heat between us makes it hard to stay away. 

Could we actually be right for each other? What happens if I ask him if he Wood Be Mine?

Revenge Plot

Stephanie Wrobel

Desperate to get his novel published, struggling writer Arnie Tenderton tracks down the literary agent who rejected him and shows up at her remote Catskills retreat over Christmas. This time, he won’t take no for an answer — because his book is about Claudia, and he’s rewriting their story. Julia Bartz says, “With its crackling tension, gasp-out-loud twists, and brilliant depictions of the line between passion and insanity, I couldn’t put this book down. Revenge Plot is an instant classic.”

Clive Cussler: Obsidian Sky

Dirk Cussler

Dirk Cussler brings his father’s most popular creation (and his own namesake) back, setting National Underwater and Marine Agency director Dirk Pitt on the trail of an ancient silver scroll written in a language older than Phoenician, with the potential to recast our understanding of history. As Pitt’s team races to decode the scroll, he’s called to investigate a wrecked freighter and discovers that the particle accelerator it was carrying — capable of ending the world — is missing. A global race to unravel these twin mysteries ensues, catapulting Pitt to exotic locations and into thrilling action as history and the future collide.

Murder of a Merry Gentleman

Celeste Connally

Bridgerton meets Agatha Christie in this dazzling fourth installment to the captivating Regency-era Lady Petra Inquires mystery series.

London, December, 1815. It’s Christmastime, and Lady Petra Forsyth is assisting the Lady Patronesses of Almack’s Assembly Rooms with four bachelor-auction dances to be held in the fortnight before Christmas Eve. With one eligible young lady per night winning the right to dance with the four eligible bachelors--called “the Merry Gentlemen” in a nod to the season--it’s sure to be a delightful event.
 
Until the first dance, when Petra and a group of science-minded young ladies discover the dead body of one of the bachelors. The death is deemed an accident, but when another bachelor’s life is nearly ended, Petra fears something sinister may be afoot. What’s more, Petra’s young friend Teddy has arrived at her door, begging for help. His long-absent mother has been imprisoned, and Teddy is certain she is innocent of her crime.
 
Time is of the essence in both cases, and Petra is asked to investigate from within by pretending to be one of the ladies vying for the bachelors’ attentions. Indeed, it’s enough to make an obstinate headstrong girl scream.
 
As she works to unravel the truth, Petra will need to act like a lady--a Lady Patroness, that is--think like an enterprising scientist, and use every investigative tactic she’s learned to solve two mysteries before she becomes the next target.

Witches of Questionable Intent

Jenn McKinlay

Zoe Ziakas is a librarian witch tasked with protecting a secret collection of enchanted books, but her world turns upside down when the dangerous Book of Shadows is stolen. Joined by her crush and their eccentric team — including an unpredictable hellhound puppy — Zoe must chase the thief through magical markets and demon-filled streets before the book’s reality-warping power spreads. Because the line between truth and illusion has begun to blur, and story of Zoe’s world is about to be rewritten… Booklist raves, “McKinlay cleverly conjures up another book-centered, magic-fueled story that brilliantly highlights her forte for wry wit and her knack for crafting suspenseful yet swoon-worthy slow-burn romances.”

Queen of Foxes

Jennifer Estep

“Exhilarating and passionate...A gripping read!” —NYT bestselling author Nalini Singh

HER ENEMIES TOOK EVERYTHING.

IT’S TIME TO STEAL IT ALL BACK.

Rinley Renard isn’t just a master thief—she’s also the sole survivor of a political coup that nearly destroyed Feronia. When the opportunity to steal a priceless sword brings Rinley back to the scene of the massacre, it’s a chance to exact her revenge—even if it means masquerading as a guard in the enemy stronghold, where she’s still a hunted fugitive.

Prince Zoren Dreiko may be the empire’s most powerful Dread Knight, but he has his own reasons for quelling the latest Feronian rebellion. Capturing the masked outlaw stirring unrest might finally free Zoren of his father’s traitorous legacy, and keep the vicious empress he serves from taking his head.

Trapped in a brutal cat-and-mouse game, Rinley and Zoren’s forbidden attraction blurs the line between duty and desire. When victory for one will doom the other, both are faced with an impossible choice between love and loyalty.

Experience Sherwood Forest like never before in this sizzling Robin Hood– inspired romantasy from New York Times bestselling author Jennifer Estep.

The Trial of Magdalena Overmorrow

Caitríona Moran

“Moran’s debut is a slow-burn romance in a historical fantasy setting, with modern political bite.” —Library Journal (starred)

Perfect for readers of Naomi Novik and Katherine Arden, The Trial of Magdalena Overmorrow is a sweeping enemies-to-lovers debut with both historical depth and fantastical allure.

Scholar. Healer. Harlot.

In her house, the villainy is her.

Magdalena Overmorrow has been called a scholar, a healer, a harlot. She carves out some measure of freedom for the women of Astoleyn, risking capture and death by caring for them and performing forbidden abortions. When she’s betrayed by a close confidante, she faces banishment to the realm’s desolate northernmost city as an accused witch. There, she must await her trial and possible doom under the watchful aegis of the Lord Proctor of Cair Gramora, a man so pious and humorless it is rumored that he has never once laughed in his life.

When she arrives, though, Magda is surprised to find that the Lord Proctor isn’t the grizzled old priest she expected but a man barely older than she is. As cold and mysterious and beautiful as the mountains at the cair’s northern border, he holds her life in his hands. One word from him could send her to the stake or worse, but she can’t help her fascination with a man and fellow scholar who is more than he appears to be, and the dangerous secrets he is clearly keeping. As her trial draws closer and the intrigue of the isolated cair threatens them both, she and the Lord Proctor must form an uneasy alliance that could either save her life or lead her to martyrdom and ruin.

This Wretched Alchemy

Tina Mars

After trying to procure a god-shard – divine fragments that bestow incredible magic –, Revel’s brother was killed and as punishment for trying to exact revenge, Revel is to fight in the Call. The Call is a battle to the death for the throne. But Revel has not been placed in the contest to secure the victory, her task is to kill the realm’s most powerful alchemist. The only problem is that he might be the only person Revel can truly trust...

Bones of Jade, Flesh Like Ice

Gracie Marsden

In 11th-century Taiwan, Yu’er is born a woman with few options and little agency. Sold into marriage, she experiences the first good luck of her life when her husband is a kind and tender man, and they develop a strong, happy bond. When that bond is broken and they are separated, Yu’er decides she will do whatever it takes to control her own destiny. She strikes a deal with a demon, and begins an implacable march toward power in the royal court. Each step of the journey costs her a portion of her humanity, but Yu’er is more than willing to pay, even as the story increasingly resembles a tragedy. Drawn from Taiwanese folklore, Yu’er’s emotional journey is unique and uniquely affecting.

Prudence Marsh Is Not a Nobody Anymore

Emily Krempholtz

When musician Prudence Marsh learns that there’s going to be an audition to play at a royal wedding, she sets out from her small village hoping to fulfill her dream of being a bard. Along the way, she bumps into handsome bandit Callum DiCorvo and his crew of men — who destroy her violin! She insists they replace it, and she’ll travel with them until they do. But when one of Callum’s jobs interferes with Prudence’s dream, will it destroy the feelings growing between them?

Too Cold for Comfort

Nisha J. Tuli

Recovering from a broken heart, photographer Aadya Williams distracts herself by traveling 1,500 miles to the Canadian Arctic to get a once-in-a-lifetime shot of a polar bear. Unfortunately, the Northern Wilderness Polar Bear Lodge is overbooked, so she is forced to stay in the family wing of the hotel with grumpy owner Reid Doerksen. The pair get off to an icy start, but when an unexpected blizzard traps Aadya and Reid together in the lodge, the freezing cold outside won’t be able to stand up to the sparks that fly between the two of them.

Hate and Other Acts of Fiction

Megan Oliver

Sadie Stockton loves her job guiding tourists through the former home of late, reclusive writer Hazel Wilmont — but she’s not excited that the new owners want to introduce a new feature to the estate. Their new plan is to host overnight murder mystery events, an idea which Sadie thinks mistreats her favorite author’s legacy, not to mention builds on the false rumors that she poisoned multiple husbands. Even worse, the new endeavor means she has to work with local bartender Ryan Pearson, the former fling she still might carry a torch for…

You, Me, and the Conspiracy

Emma Barry

Jessica Wilson is desperate to find a new topic for her next book, after the disastrous rejection of her latest work threatens her tenure path. When she stumbles upon a centuries-old mystery involving the United States’ Founding Fathers, she recruits adjunct professor Calloway Morgan to help with her investigation… and finds equal parts love and adventure in the process.

The Runner

Scarlett Thomas

Jay has spent decades running from a contract on his life when he meets Ellie, a fellow runner with secrets of her own. After an assassin tracks him to a resort, the pair flee together, forcing Jay to choose between the woman he’s falling for and the survival instincts that have kept him alive. Publishers Weekly says, “Catch-22 meets The White Lotus in this thrillingly absurd tale of heretics, heisters, and hit men… It’s a wild ride.”

When They Find Me

Carter Wilson

Annie Wolfe has gone off-grid in the remote Colorado town of Expanse, determined to protect her daughter from the people hunting them. Then Riven arrives with her survivalist family, seeking revenge against a man from their past. When the two women cross paths, the truth will turn out to be more dangerous than either of them realize. New York Times bestselling author Tess Gerritsen says, “Carter Wilson delivers the heart-pounding suspense of a true thriller. You won’t be able to put this one down.”

Before I Disappear

Cate Quinn

Criminologist April Anderson wakes up in a remote motel with a new identity and no memory of the crime that will force her to stand witness in a major trial. As she struggles to trust the police officer protecting her or the fiancé secretly tracking her, fragments of her past begin to reveal a disturbing side of herself. With the trial approaching and someone determined to silence her, April must uncover the truth before her missing memories cost her her life.

Everything Happens So Much

Andrew H. Murray

Esme Good is stuck in a dull job and an even duller life, escaping into alternate realities with mysterious potions that let her briefly experience other versions of herself. But after an ordinary workplace mishap makes her the key to saving the universe, Esme is forced into an adventure involving a long-forgotten prophecy and an unexplored world. Publishers Weekly calls Everything Happens So Much “an entertaining thrill-ride” with “clever comedic writing on every page.”

Swipe Bite

Alexandra Vasti

Vampire heiress Sophronia Vega has helped create Stokr, a dating app designed to safely match vampires with humans. But when the app is sabotaged and dates turn deadly, she teams up with human software engineer Casey Amato to find the culprit. As they investigate someone within Sophronia’s inner circle, their growing attraction makes their partnership even more complicated — and potentially dangerous. New York Times bestselling author Deanna Raybourn praises this fun paranormal romance as “fresh, fully creative, and completely plausible.” 

Thunderbird Ranch

Laura Griffin

A year after the mysterious disappearance of his father, Will brings his fiancée, Lilian, to his family’s Texas ranch to celebrate his mother’s birthday. When they arrive, however, his mother announces that she’s marrying their long-time neighbor Cal, who everyone hates. Before anyone can process the news, Cal turns up dead — shot multiple times and with an axe in his back. Just about everyone in the family is a suspect, and rookie homicide detective Kate Graham has her hands full trying to figure out who’s lying and who’s telling the truth in this twisty tale.

Peregrine Hill

Nina de Gramont

After losing her husband and three of her children in a tragic shipwreck, Isabelle Bishop thinks she has found security again in John Whitten, a wealthy scion in early 20th-century New York City — but she soon discovers that John’s attentions are not for her but for her 18-year-old daughter, Mariah, as he begins blackmailing them with his knowledge of a scandal in Mariah’s past to arrange a marriage. Joining forces with her kind and driven maid, Hetty, Mariah finds a way to fight for the future she truly wants. Nita Prose says, “The Gilded Age springs to vivid life in [the] pages” of this “luminous, entrancing novel.”

The Unfinished Work

Jeff Shaara

Bestselling novelist Jeff Shaara, author of Gods and Generals and The Rising Tide, brings his unique combination of meticulous historical scholarship and captivating storytelling to explore the life of celebrated President Abraham Lincoln. During his years in the White House, Lincoln was determined to move the nation from conflict to reconciliation and renewed prosperity — but paid the ultimate price for being the figurehead of the Union. Ken Burns says, “I can’t think of anyone who gets to the heart of the Civil War quite like Jeff Shaara does in his wonderful novels.” 

Bad Company: A Thriller

Sara Paretsky

Seventysomething Chicago retiree Lily Sedako appears to lead an ordinary life, but she is hiding a past as a CIA field agent whose work in Central Asia ended in political upheaval and a deadly coup. When an anonymous package threatens to expose her long-buried secrets, Lily must draw on her old skills and connections to uncover who is targeting her — and what really happened more than two decades ago. Harlan Coben says, “Sara Paretsky is a legend… If you haven’t read her yet, now is the time.”

The Body in the Bath

Ragnar Jónasson

As detective Helgi Reykdal prepares to return to work in Reykjavík, he is still reeling from the death of his girlfriend in a crash caused by his troubled ex, Bergþóra. Seeking an escape from his grief, he throws himself into the long-unsolved disappearance of retired detective Hulda. But when Bergþóra is later found dead — and suspicion falls on Helgi himself — the two cases begin to collide in unexpected ways…

The Cold Read

Tara Laskowski

Ten years after a horror film made them stars, four former castmates reunite at the remote ski resort where it was filmed to announce a sequel. But when a disturbing incident brings their friend’s death back to the surface, old secrets and resentments threaten to derail the reunion. With everyone hiding something and a killer seemingly among them, they’ll have to figure out who they can trust before the weekend turns deadly. In a starred review, Booklist says, “Laskowski’s homage to classic horror tropes, slasher films, and the devoted fandom they cultivate is a sharply written page-turner that readers will be hard-pressed to put down.”

The Key Biscayne Affair

Xita Rubert

After a custody battle, an unnamed narrator and her brother move with their eccentric Spanish father from Boston to Key Biscayne. As their father becomes increasingly reckless and absorbed in the island’s glamorous social scene, the children are pulled deeper into his unstable world, with his daughter gradually shifting from observer to willing accomplice. In a starred review, Kirkus Reviews says, “This little diamond, a philosophical comedy, is a fever dream of childhood.”
